news.title:
Himatsingka Seide Q4 FY26 revenue rises 5.8% YoY to INR 721 Cr.
Firm plans diversification, 850 Cr debt raise, and capacity utilization varies across segments.

Himatsingka Seide's board approved audited financial results for FY26 and recommended a final dividend of Rs 0.25/share.
The company reported unmodified audit opinions for both standalone and consolidated accounts and completed its Secretarial Audit Report.
Full year 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹4.93 (vs ₹6.92 in FY 2025)
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹4.93 (down from ₹6.92 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹27.3b (down 1.8% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹619.6m (down 19% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 2.3% (down from 2.7% in FY 2025). The decrease in margin was driven by lower revenue. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 17% per year but the company’s share price has fallen by 8% per year, which means it is significantly lagging earnings.

news.title: Himatsingka Seide Limited Recommends Final Dividend for the Financial Year Ended 2025-26
news.body: Himatsingka Seide Limited at the board meeting held on May 27, 2026, Recommended Final Dividend of INR 0.25 per equity share (5%) of face value INR 5/- each for the Financial Year ended 2025-26, subject to the approval of shareholders at the ensuing Annual General Meeting of the Company.

news.title: Himatsingka Seide Limited announced that it expects to receive INR 5.5 billion in funding
news.body: Himatsingka Seide Limited announced a private placement to issue 55,000 series “1” INR denominated, senior, secured, rated, listed, redeemable, taxable, non-convertible debenture for gross proceeds of INR 550 million on May 27, 2026. The transaction will include participation from eligible investors. The transaction will be completed in one or more tranches and has been approved by the board of the directors of the company. The tenure of the debt is 42 months from the deemed date of allotment and will have an interest rate of 11.50% p.a., payable quarterly. The principal amount will be repaid in three instalments at the end of 30 months, 36 months and 42 months respectively. The company can raise INR 2,500 million with series "1" non convertible debentures through Green Shoe Option .

news.title: New minor risk - Market cap size
news.body: The company's market capitalization is less than US$100m. Market cap: ₹9.56b (US$99.8m) This is considered a minor risk. Companies with a small market capitalization are most likely businesses that have not yet released a product to market or are simply a very small company without a wide reach. Either way, risk is elevated with these companies because there is a chance the product may not come to fruition or the company's addressable market or demand may not be as large as expected. In addition, if the company's size is the main factor, it is less likely to have many investors and analysts following it and scrutinizing its performance and outlook. news.title: New minor risk - Share price stability
news.body: The company's share price has been volatile over the past 3 months. It is more volatile than 75% of Indian stocks, typically moving 7.7% a week. This is considered a minor risk. Share price volatility indicates the stock is highly sensitive to market conditions or economic conditions rather than being sensitive to its own business performance, which may also be inconsistent. It also increases the risk of potential losses in the short term as the stock tends to have larger drops in price more frequently than other stocks. news.body: The company has an unstable dividend paying track record. The dividend has had an annual drop of over 20% in the past. Dividend yield: 0.3% This is considered a minor risk.
